abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the joint space is a suitable environment for embryonic stem (ES) cells to grow and form cartilage. METHOD: We transplanted ES cells into the knee joint and a subcutaneous space of mice with severe combined immunodeficiency. RESULTS: Teratomas formed in both areas. Those in the joints grew and destroyed the joints. The incidence of cartilage formation was the same in the knee joint and subcutaneous space, but the ratio of cartilage to teratoma was higher in the knee joint than in the subcutaneous space. The teratomas were proved to have been derived from the transplanted ES cells by detection of the neomycin-resistance gene that had been transfected into the ES cells. CONCLUSIONS: It is currently not possible to use ES cells to repair joint tissues. Further optimization of donor ES cells to differentiate as well as inhibit tumour growth may help to meet these challenges.
abstract_ja: 目的：関節腔がES細胞の増殖と軟骨形成に適した環境であるかを確かめること。方法：ES細胞を重症複合免疫不全（SCID）マウスの膝関節と皮下に移植した。結果：両部位で奇形腫が形成された。関節内のものは増殖して関節を破壊した。軟骨形成の頻度は両部位で同程度であったが、奇形腫に対する軟骨の比率は皮下より膝関節で高かった。奇形腫は、移植ES細胞に導入されたネオマイシン耐性遺伝子の検出により、移植細胞に由来することが証明された。結論：現時点ではES細胞を関節組織の修復に用いることはできない。腫瘍増殖を抑えるとともに分化を促すためには、ドナーES細胞のさらなる最適化が役立つ可能性がある。
